headline: BBC seeks to subpoena Trump family members in $10bn defamation suit
standfirst: The broadcaster wants testimony from Ivanka Trump, Donald Trump Jr. and Jared Kushner about the president's January 6 speech.

paragraphs.text: The BBC has asked a United States court for assistance in obtaining testimony from members of Donald Trump's family in the defamation suit brought over its Panorama programme, according to reports published on 16 August 2026. The broadcaster is seeking to subpoena Ivanka Trump, Donald Trump Jr. and Jared Kushner to testify about Trump's January 6 speech as part of the $10bn lawsuit, those reports said.
Courts have blocked construction of Trump's White House ballroom. The administration has asked the Supreme Court to allow the construction to continue.

Trump ordered changes to the recommended childhood vaccination schedule, with health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. present. Sen. Bill Cassidy, Republican of Louisiana, said the executive order altering the schedule is based on "crazy, stupid" claims, and said it is why Trump's poll numbers are falling.
According to a report published on 16 August 2026, a new poll finds most voters say they are worse off under Trump.

More than 5.3 million individuals across the country have lost SNAP benefits since Trump enacted major overhauls to the programme in his 2025 tax and spending law, according to U.S. Department of Agriculture figures. Massachusetts' Department of Transitional Assistance reported that SNAP enrollment in the state dropped by nearly 182,000 individuals, including roughly 65,000 children. The same department reported that daily call volume has risen 9% year on year, with roughly 47% of callers unable to connect, up from 37%.

The 20% pass-through business income deduction, increased from 17% during the 2017 Tax Cut and Jobs Act negotiations and made permanent in last year's One Big Beautiful Bill Act, will cost the budget $820bn over a 10-year period, almost as much as was cut from Medicaid. About 57% of the $1.3tn in pass-through income in 2022 went to 890,000 people in the richest 1% of the population, according to the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center. The deduction leaves top pass-through owners taxed at 29.6% against a 37% top marginal rate on wages.

NPR reported on 16 August 2026 that the Trump administration's continuing actions targeting transgender youth, including a change to Medicaid, are taking a personal toll on affected families, as described by a longtime Republican voter living in California.

Trump signed a memorandum authorizing U.S. private-sector companies to launch offensive cyberattacks against foreign cybercriminals. The memo was reported on 15 August 2026 by NPR, The Guardian, The Washington Post and The New York Times.
Colombia's president has asked Trump to suspend tariffs to assist earthquake recovery.

Trump drew criticism over the weekend of 15-16 August 2026 after sharing a black-and-white image of himself wearing a "Trump 2028" hat with the message "We are going to win," despite the 22nd Amendment's limit on presidential terms. Asked at Joint Base Andrews on Tuesday, 11 August 2026, whether he was serious about seeking a third term, Trump said: "And you know that the law is very strong on that. I'd love to run, but the law is very strong." He then ignored a reporter's attempt to press further.

The BBC reported that on 8 July 2026 Trump boarded Air Force One in view of television cameras as he left the Nato summit in Turkey, but was spirited away via a catering truck to a C-32A that flew him to RAF Mildenhall, leaving unwitting decoys aboard the larger aircraft. In remarks to reporters reported by the BBC on 12 August 2026, Trump confirmed that he secretly swapped planes as he left the summit because of a possible threat.
